## Visualizing the Entropy of the Poisson Distribution

This R script calculates and visualizes the entropy of the Poisson distribution as a function of the rate parameter $\lambda$. The entropy is computed numerically by summing over the distribution’s Probability Mass Function (PMF), quantifying the uncertainty in predicting the number of events within a fixed interval. The script generates a line plot of entropy versus $\lambda$, highlighting how entropy increases as $\lambda$ grows, reflecting greater variability in outcomes. An example point (e.g., $\lambda$ = 3) is emphasized on the plot to show the approximate entropy value for a specific case.

```{r setup, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
# Entropy of Poisson Distribution Visualization

# Function to compute entropy of Poisson
poisson_entropy <- function(lambda, max_y = 100) {
  y <- 0:max_y
  probs <- dpois(y, lambda)
  entropy <- -sum(probs * log(probs), na.rm = TRUE)
  return(entropy)
}

# Compute entropy values for a range of lambda
lambda_values <- seq(0.5, 20, by = 0.5)
entropy_values <- sapply(lambda_values, poisson_entropy)

# Plot entropy vs. lambda
plot(lambda_values, entropy_values, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "blue",
     xlab = expression(lambda), ylab = "Entropy (nats)",
     main = "Entropy of the Poisson Distribution")

# Highlight a specific point, e.g., lambda = 3
lambda_point <- 3
entropy_point <- poisson_entropy(lambda_point)
points(lambda_point, entropy_point, col = "red", pch = 19)
text(lambda_point, entropy_point + 0.2,
     labels = paste0("λ = ", lambda_point, "\nH ≈ ", round(entropy_point, 3)),
     col = "red")
```
